lines.text: name: vitadeck-emulator

description: Runs the VitaDeck Vita build (VPK) in the Vita3K emulator on macOS, Windows or Linux, sets the emulator up on a new machine, and drives it. Use when the user mentions Vita3K, the emulator, testing the Vita build without the device, libshacccg.suprx, or running the VPK on a computer.
metadata:
internal: true
# VitaDeck in Vita3K
`scripts/vita3k.sh` runs the Vita build without the device. It builds JS and the VPK (Docker), installs the VPK and the example Deck Apps into [Vita3K](https://vita3k.org), and launches it:
```sh
scripts/vita3k.sh          # build, then launch
scripts/vita3k.sh launch   # launch the existing out-vita/vitadeck.vpk

Emulator config and storage live in `~/.vitadeck/vita3k` (`VITADECK_VITA3K_HOME`), shared by every worktree. `fs/` in there is the emulated Vita: `ux0/data/vitadeck` is the VitaDeck Data Root, `ur0/data` holds the shader compiler. Run `scripts/vita3k.sh help` for the environment variables.
## Set up a new machine
1. Install the Vita build prerequisites: Node.js 22+, pnpm, Docker (see `vitadeck-build`). `scripts/vita3k.sh` uses `docker compose`.
2. Install Vita3K:
- macOS: download the dmg from [vita3k.org](https://vita3k.org) for your CPU (Intel or Apple silicon) and drag `Vita3K.app` to Applications.
- Windows: `winget install Vita3K.Vita3K`, then run the script from Git Bash. If Vita3K isn't on PATH, set `VITA3K` to `Vita3K.exe`.
- Linux: download the AppImage, `chmod +x` it, and set `VITA3K` to it.

3. Install `libshacccg.suprx`. vitaGL compiles its shaders at runtime with Sony's shader compiler, which can't be redistributed, so it isn't in the repo and the script won't launch without it. Use one of:
- Copy it from a machine that already runs VitaDeck in Vita3K: `scp <machine>:.vitadeck/vita3k/fs/ur0/data/libshacccg.suprx /tmp/ && scripts/vita3k.sh shacccg /tmp/libshacccg.suprx`.

- Download it from the Vita: run [ShaRKBR33D](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/ShaRKBR33D) on the Vita once (it extracts the decrypted module to `ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx`), start VitaShell's FTP server, then `PSVITAIP=<ip> scripts/vita3k.sh shacccg`.

4. Optional: install the firmware. VitaDeck runs without it; it only provides the CA list that `fetch` reads (fetch still fails, see below). `Vita3K --firmware PSVUPDAT.PUP` installs into Vita3K's default storage and ignores our config, so move `os0` and `vs0` from there into `~/.vitadeck/vita3k/fs/` afterwards. On macOS that is `~/Library/Application Support/Vita3K/Vita3K/fs`.
5. `scripts/vita3k.sh`. The first launch installs the VPK; the Demo Deck App should appear.
## Controls
| Vita | Vita3K keyboard |
| D-pad | Arrow keys |
| Start (opens the VitaDeck Shell) | Enter |
| Cross | X |
| Circle | C |
| Square / Triangle | Z / V |
| L / R | Q / E |
| Select | Right Shift |
Start is Enter here, not F1 as in the host build.
## Driving it as an agent
- Click the Vita3K window once before sending keys. Keys sent while it is merely frontmost are dropped.
- Hold each key for about 60 ms. Longer holds trigger VitaDeck's D-pad repeat and overshoot the focus.
- The VitaDeck log is in the terminal as `export_sceClibVprintf` lines. An access violation at `0x80` logged at startup is harmless.
- Runtime Upload works: open Upload in the Shell, then `vitadeck dev http://127.0.0.1:8787/` or `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/upload -F archive=@<app>.vdapp.zip` from the same machine.
## Known emulator gaps
These are Vita3K bugs, not VitaDeck bugs. Check them on the device.

- HTTPS `fetch` fails with a certificate name mismatch. Vita3K's `sceNetInetPton` returns an error instead of 0 for host names, so curl skips SNI. Without the firmware it fails earlier, on the missing `vs0:` CA list.
- The Vita keyboard dialog (Text Input) opens but takes no input.

lines.text: `upload_vpk` copies the VPK to `ux0:/download/` for a manual install. `upload_vita` (and `run`) stops the running app, uploads `eboot.bin`, the runtime and the fonts, then relaunches. It also uploads `assets/emoji` (about 4,000 PNGs in one curl run), but only the first time per build directory and Vita IP and again when the images change, tracked by `out-vita/upload_emoji-<ip>.stamp`; delete that stamp to force a re-upload, e.g. after removing the app from the Vita.
Without the device, run the VPK in the Vita3K emulator with `scripts/vita3k.sh` (skill `vitadeck-emulator`).
## Workflows
### Canonical agent checks
- `js/examples/` - example Deck Apps; `smoke` is the CI smoke fixture
- `tests/` - CTest harnesses (`smoke_harness.c`, `package_manifest_harness.c`, `package_library_harness.c`, `timer_reload_harness.c`, `upload_parsing_harness.c`) and golden screenshots
- `vendor/quickjs` - git submodule; `docker-compose.yml` + `Dockerfile` - Vitasdk and Linux smoke images

- `.agents/skills/` - repo skills (`vitadeck-build`, `vitadeck-smoke`, `vitadeck-manual-testing`, `vitadeck-vdapp-upload`, `vitadeck-deck-app-init`) plus `comprehende` installed from `matemolnar8/comprehende` via the `skills` CLI (`skills-lock.json`) and `pages`, a repo-owned skill with its own publish script. `.claude/skills` symlinks here. Published via `npx skills add matemolnar8/vitadeck`.

- `.agents/skills/` - repo skills (`vitadeck-build`, `vitadeck-emulator`, `vitadeck-smoke`, `vitadeck-manual-testing`, `vitadeck-vdapp-upload`, `vitadeck-deck-app-init`) plus `comprehende` installed from `matemolnar8/comprehende` via the `skills` CLI (`skills-lock.json`) and `pages`, a repo-owned skill with its own publish script. `.claude/skills` symlinks here. Published via `npx skills add matemolnar8/vitadeck`.
## Setup
- Vita build and Linux smoke run in Docker. Start Docker Desktop first.

- The first CMake configure downloads the pinned runtime fonts and Twemoji images ([cmake/fonts.cmake](cmake/fonts.cmake), [cmake/twemoji.cmake](cmake/twemoji.cmake)) into the gitignored `assets/fonts/` and `assets/emoji/`; offline it warns, builds anyway with fallbacks (raylib's built-in font, missing-glyph boxes for CJK and Korean, a fallback glyph for emoji), and the next configure retries.
- Uploading a Vita build (`upload_vita`, `upload_vpk`, `run`) reads the Vita's IP from `PSVITAIP` when CMake configures, e.g. `export PSVITAIP=192.168.1.177`.

- Without the device, `scripts/vita3k.sh` builds the VPK and runs it in the [Vita3K](https://vita3k.org) emulator (macOS, Windows via Git Bash, Linux) with the example Deck Apps installed. New machine setup (Vita3K, Sony's shader compiler) and controls: [the `vitadeck-emulator` skill](.agents/skills/vitadeck-emulator/SKILL.md). Start is Enter in Vita3K, not F1.
- Releases: [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md).
